findings.title: Check your wallet: Woolworths shoppers hit by digital gift card theft
findings.summary_md: Nine reported that dozens of Woolworths customers had WISH eGift card balances drained, sometimes discovered only when they tried to pay at checkout. Customers quoted by Nine described cards shown as redeemed, purchases at Dan Murphy's and Big W often in another state, and long waits on the gift card support line. One shopper bought a $500 card, spent about $130 in Melbourne and found the remaining $367 spent in New South Wales three days later.

findings.title: Coles calls in global experts after 'cyber security incident'
findings.summary_md: The Daily Mail reported that Coles had brought in global cyber security experts to contain and secure its IT environment after detecting a cyber security incident. Coles said it had not identified evidence that customer, team or supplier data had been compromised or removed, and that it was working with the Australian Cyber Security Centre and regulators. The company told customers to be alert to unexpected emails and SMS messages and said it would never ask for passwords through unsolicited messages.

findings.title: Coles suffers cybersecurity incident
findings.summary_md: Nine reported that Coles was investigating a cybersecurity incident while stores, the website and app, Flybuys and gift cards remained usable. Coles acknowledged issues with Liquorland click-and-collect for a small number of customers and said it had found no evidence that customer, team or supplier data was compromised. The company said it was working with the Australian Cyber Security Centre and global cybersecurity experts, and advised customers to watch for suspicious links and SMS messages.

findings.title: Coles investigating breach amid rise in 'incidents' overseas
findings.summary_md: Yahoo News reported that Coles had opened an investigation with government authorities and international cyber security experts and had found no evidence that sensitive information was accessed. The company gave no detection time, attack method or affected systems, and said supermarket operations and self-service checkouts were continuing. The report placed the disclosure two weeks after attacks in Europe in which hackers manipulated supermarket refrigeration systems and caused food spoilage.

findings.title: Woolworths shoppers find gift cards drained in interstate transactions
findings.summary_md: The Daily Mail reported Woolworths shoppers finding hundreds of dollars missing from WISH eGift cards through interstate transactions, with some card purchases made through third-party platforms such as Qantas Marketplace. One customer in Karratha said she learned of the loss at checkout and struggled to reach the gift card line; another in regional Queensland said she called 13 times. Woolworths told the outlet it was looking into the matter as a priority and said replacement cards were among the next steps for affected customers.

findings.title: Woolies shopper the latest victim of gift card tampering
findings.summary_md: Nine reported in June 2026 that a Woolworths shopper found redemption details and part of the serial number scratched off Apple gift cards bought in store, while a Coles customer said she was $2,000 out of pocket over four tampered cards loaded with $500 each. Woolworths said a very small number of its gift cards had been affected by tampering, that it had introduced stronger in-store security and packaging, and that it was working with law enforcement and suppliers. The ACCC urged gift card providers to maintain systems that prevent fraud and said customers should seek refunds or replacements from the retailer with proof of purchase.
